A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIFT research, with matching methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices were readable and support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LooGLE and LongBench results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and NIAH experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results, replaces the efficiency experiment, and adds an original attention-output analysis in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Overlapping segmentation, auxiliary QA, contextualized training, and the two-MLP Gated Memory adapter remain unchanged. The added implementation explanations and experimental context-access conditions do not establish a changed algorithm, objective, or architecture.

E1.justification: LooGLE, the same five LongBench subtasks, and NIAH are retained; NIAH moves from Appendix B to C. Appendix D narrowly extends tested input conditions by explicitly comparing document-free and full-document inputs on one LooGLE ShortQA document, without adding a dataset or domain.

E2.justification: The reported Figure 4 comparison changes from ICL, PiSSA, and Gated Memory to ICL, LIFT, and an idealized LIFT (Llama 3.1) condition. Although v3's setup still mentions PiSSA efficiency comparisons, its timing series is absent from the replacement figure. Main benchmark and adapter-ablation comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 4.2.3 replaces timing a single NIAH task across input lengths with generation-time measurements across output lengths at fixed 20K, 50K, and 100K inputs, including an idealized condition without truncated ICL. Appendix D adds answer-token cosine-similarity measurements with full-context and document-free controls. An evaluator switch is unresolved: v3 Section 4.1 retains GPT4-0613, while its new Appendix B.2 names GPT-3.5-turbo-0125.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 6 add a limited, single-document diagnostic testing whether end-to-end Gated Memory reproduces full-context attention. Existing contextualized-training, auxiliary-QA-count, adapter, in/out-context, and NIAH analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates, and the decoding-randomness descriptions are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces input-scaling results, including the reported 90K memory limit and above-800K PiSSA timing crossover, with generation-length curves and a reported crossover beyond approximately 1500 generated tokens under different conditions. Figure 6 newly shows lower full-context attention similarity for Gated Memory than for the base model. Table 2 changes Llama 3 LIFT ShortQA from 48.84 to 47.51, matching the existing 10-QA result; 48.84 remains the 30-QA result in Table 5.

T1.justification: The objectives and attention decomposition in Equations 1–7 retain their mathematical substance. Indexing context as c_k and correcting the attention function's third argument clarify notation. Appendix D provides empirical evidence, without adding a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of storing long inputs in parameters, improving short-context LLM performance, and balancing parametric memory with ICL through Gated Memory. The introduction additionally mentions the already-existing contextualized-training component.

C2.justification: The efficiency discussion shifts from substantial adaptation overhead and delayed crossover to emphasizing decoding advantages after sufficiently long generation. Section 6 replaces the auxiliary-task emphasis on minimal benefit and overfitting with benefits constrained by computational cost and task alignment. Appendix D newly qualifies the mechanism: trained Gated Memory does not reproduce full-context attention, motivating future distillation experiments.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies 2048-token segments, a 768-token stride, independently sampled 4096-token contextual prefixes/suffixes, the recitation prompt, and supervision restricted to the target segment. Appendix B.2 adds the evaluation prompt, and Appendix D specifies diagnostic inputs and token selection. These are chiefly disclosures; existing hyperparameter and GPU-cost tables are retained under reordered numbering.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused comparison with Wang et al. (2024b), distinguishing inference-time training for long generation from LIFT's understanding tasks and Gated Memory adapter. v3 also adds the accounting-document citation to Li et al. (2024), while removing Focused Transformer and LongQLoRA citations. The broader positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes widespread light copyedits, removes the duplicated opening explanation in Section 3.2, clarifies terminology, and reorganizes implementation details and prompts into separate appendices. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redrawn with revised styling, labels, and arrangement. Figure 4 changes from one input-scaling plot to three generation-length panels with an inset, and Figure 6 adds an attention-similarity plot. Appendix tables and prompt boxes are rearranged; the NIAH heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit training recipe, evaluation prompt, attention diagnostic, and Table 2 alignment improve transparency and consistency. However, the new appendix contradicts Section 4.1 about the evaluation model, and the revised efficiency discussion removes earlier adaptation-cost qualifications while making broader efficiency assertions under different conditions. These material gains and losses leave the net change in paper quality uncertain.
